question: is the DMS-trained, predictor-free scorer faster than AlphaMissense and ESM1b?
honest_answer: not in any way a user would feel, and the framing is misleading. See accounting below.

accounting.the_scorer_is_not_small: it is a gradient-boosted tree head on ProtT5-XL, a 3B-parameter transformer. The trees are ~MB; the frontend is not.
accounting.vs_esm1b_end_to_end: ProtT5-XL at 3B parameters is LARGER than ESM1b at 650M, so on a novel sequence this scorer needs more compute, not less
accounting.vs_alphamissense_in_practice: AlphaMissense and ESM1b ship as precomputed proteome-wide score files. For any human protein a user's cost is a lookup, not a forward pass, so there is no inference time to beat
accounting.where_speed_could_matter: sequences outside those released files -- engineered proteins, other organisms -- and there this scorer is the heavier option, not the lighter one

not_measured_here.prot_t5_forward_pass: no GPU in this session; the project's own prior measurement is cited instead

prior_measurement.source: beat_am run log, route B embedding stage

not_measured_here.alphamissense_inference: weights are not runnable without AlphaFold-scale infrastructure; only released predictions were used anywhere in this project
